subject: Discovery recap & next steps — embeddings / reranking for BrightCart
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@brightcart.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — embeddings / reranking for BrightCart

Hi Samir — great to meet you and Maya today, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Key pain points you shared:
- Search relevance for long-tail / seasonal SKUs is inconsistent, hurting conversion on recommendations.
- Current reranking approach (rules + ML hybrid) struggles with cold-start SKUs and query understanding for complex queries.
- Cost and latency for your current rerank flow spike during promotions.

Current stack you described:
- Vector DB: Pinecone (serverless) for ANN index, metadata in Postgres.
- Embeddings: 768-d vectors (offline batch generation), stored in Pinecone; ~9.2M vectors today.
- Rerank: business rules + small in-house model for final scoring.
- Ingestion: nightly bulk updates + ad-hoc bursts during promotions.

Scale & traffic (as discussed):
- Index size: ~9.2M product vectors (768-d).
- Ingestion pattern: nightly batch (~50–100k updates), promotional bursts up to ~200k/day.
- Query patterns: baseline ~80 QPS, typical peak ~420 QPS during promotions.

Success criteria you’re targeting:
- Improve top-1 CTR for search & recommendations by >= 6% (vs current baseline).
- End-to-end p95 latency for retrieval + rerank: target <120 ms (ideal target <100 ms for user-facing scenarios).
- Keep incremental cost for rerank + retrieval under your threshold (we discussed target < $0.50 / 1k queries as a starting point to evaluate against).

Our recommended pilot approach (high level):
1) Retrieval + hybrid rerank POC — run ANN retrieval (top-50) in Pinecone and then use Redwood-hosted rerank model (prompt or fine-tuned) to score the top candidates.
2) Measure: top-1 CTR, CTR@5, latency p50/p95, and cost per 1k queries.
3) Optimize: batch patterns, KV caching for frequent prefixes, and quantized rerank models to meet latency/cost SLOs.

Immediate next steps we agreed:
- You to share a small sample dataset (schema + ~50k product vectors or a CSV of representative metadata).
- We’ll run an initial cost/latency sketch for a 9.2M index and your peak QPS profile.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45 min) with your infra/search engineer (Maya) and our infra team (Aditya + Monica) week of July 6.
- Build a mutual action plan (timeline + success metrics) for a 4-week POC.

Attachments: brightcart-analytics-overview.pdf (high-level traffic and KPIs you mentioned).

If I missed anything or any numbers above need correction, please flag and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll coordinate with Aditya and Monica to propose slots for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Note: will prepare a short cost sketch for the 9.2M vector profile ahead of the deep-dive.

From: Samir Patel <samir.p@brightcart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@brightcart.com>, search-team@brightcart.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:43:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — embeddings / reranking for BrightCart

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. Couple clarifications / additions from our side: 
- Index size: current snapshot is 9.2M vectors (we do keep historical variants, but POC should focus on current live SKUs).
- Embedding dim: 768 (we currently use an in-house encoder; open to moving to an off-the-shelf model if it improves quality).
- Ingestion: baseline nightly job ~60k updates, promotions can push to ~200k updates/day (workers spawn during peak windows).
- QPS: baseline ~80 QPS, sustained peak ~420 QPS for 20–40 min bursts during heavy traffic (flash sales).
- Latency expectations: we are flexible but want p95 end-to-end retrieval + rerank under 120 ms for the UX team (ideally 80–100 ms).

POC timeline: we’d like a 4-week POC that demonstrates improved relevance on a 10% sample of traffic, with clear gating metrics so we can decide on roll-out. Maya (CTO) is copied — she’ll join the tech deep-dive.

Attachments: brightcart-traffic-screenshot.png (traffic profile / peak windows).

Questions for Redwood before the deep-dive:
1) Can you share an architecture sketch for retrieval + rerank at our scale (9.2M vectors, peaks up to ~420 QPS)?
2) Rough cost estimate (ballpark) for the POC: retrieval (Pinecone) + Redwood rerank per 1k queries for our expected load.
3) Any limitations on batch ingestion size or real-time update patterns we should know about?

Appreciate the quick follow-up — Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Search, BrightCart
samir.p@brightcart.com | +1 (312) 555-2210
